decoDesc.decoNote: Folios 1b and 2a form a fully illuminated, symmetrical double-page frontispiece opening set within multi-layered geometric frames. Each page is organized around a large rectangular upper panel, a horizontal cartouche immediately below it and above the main text block, the text block itself, and a second horizontal cartouche below it. Surmounting the text area is a large, rectangular illuminated headpiece, enclosed within a border system of minium and malachite green rulings. At the center of the headpiece sits a prominent lobed ogival medallion in minium on a deep lapis lazuli blue ground, adorned with fine gold arabesque scrollwork, and flanked along the outer vertical edges by two matching half-medallions of similar design and color. Along the bottom edge of the panel, the composition features a central upward-pointing cruciform half-medallion, flanked by two stylized, bird-like floral pendants above and two lobed quarter-medallions at the lower corners—all uniformly set against a deep lapis lazuli ground. Along the top edge of the headpiece, a series of pointed, flame-like crests in gold project upward into the unilluminated upper margin. The upper horizontal cartouches function as surah headings, formatted as elongated rectangular panels with burnished gold leaf grounds flanked by gilt diamond spandrels at the outer edges. The right-hand cartouche contains the inscription سورة الفاتحة الکتاب سبع آية نزل مكیّه. The corresponding cartouche on the left contains the title and verse count of the following sūra: سورة البقره آیات ستّه و ثمانون آية مدینه. Both panels are enclosed by a narrow minium (vermilion) band along the top and a delicate white-lead fretwork/meander band along the bottom. The central text block is arranged in horizontal registers delimited by fine line rulings, featuring black calligraphic script executed within reserved, undulating cloud-shaped outlines (cloud-band reserves) on the natural cream paper substrate. Surrounding these reserves, an extensive field of burnished gold leaf fills the entire rectangular text panel—occupying all interlinear spaces and margins around the script. Enclosing the entire central block and headpiece along the outer margins is a wide border (hashiya). It displays a reciprocal pattern of interlocking, lobed cloud-band cartouches alternating between deep lapis lazuli blue fields decorated with white-lead arabesque spirals (islimi) and burnished gold fields ornamented with symmetrical orange and white rosettes. The lower horizontal cartouches are similarly elongated and rectangular, with gilt grounds and elaborate floral decoration. Each contains a calligraphic inscription in the centre, surrounded by scrolling floral ornament and enclosed by turquoise, minium, and gilt bands. The right-hand cartouche contains the inscription لا يمسه الا المطهرون تنزیل من رب العالمین کاتبه محمد صادق. The corresponding cartouche on the left contains the same text without the reference to the scribe, لا يمسه الا المطهرون تنزیل من رب العالمین. Enclosing the central decorative unit and its multi-line framing system, the wide outer margin border (hashiya) displays on three sides a dynamic reciprocal pattern of undulating, interlocking lobed cloud-bands. These alternating fields seamlessly shift between two distinct grounds: deep lapis lazuli blue fields decorated with delicate white lead arabesque spirals (islimi) punctuated by vermilion accents, and gleaming burnished gold fields ornamented with symmetrical five-petaled rosettes in vermilion and white lead with ultra-fine lapis blue tendrils.

In contrast to the lavishly illuminated opening pages, the following pages feature a clean, functional layout without gold leaf illumination. They present a structured, rectangular text block enclosed within a simple multi-line framing system consisting of fine, parallel rulings in minium, lapis lazuli blue, and black ink. The internal text area is organized into neat horizontal registers separated by fine rule lines, with each surah introduced by a narrow, full-width rectangular header panel defined by upper and lower ruling lines. The main body text is formatted in uniform, horizontal lines bounded precisely by the vertical outer rulings of the frame. The entire text block is framed by a double-ruled decorative border. Finally, the layout of the leaves is completed by a single black decorative frame that runs consistently along the outer margins of all subsequent pages.

bindingDesc.p: Brown leather binding, 19 × 30 cm, front + back cover, leather + pasteboard.
bindingDesc.decoNote: The exterior boards are decorated with blind-tooled rectangular frames formed by parallel ruled lines. A narrow fretwork border runs along the perimeter, with additional ruled compartments at the head and tail of the board.
bindingDesc.condition: The leather surface is extensively abraded and scuffed, with areas of surface loss and staining. The board edges and corners show pronounced wear consistent with age and handling.

history.acquisition: Donated to The Ferdowsi Library by Dr Caro Minasian in 1972.

recordHist.source: This record was created by Dr Mohammad Emami based on the information published in the Persian catalogue by Dr Ali Mir-Ansari (Catalogue of the Persian and Arabic Manuscripts in the Ferdowsi Library, Wadham College, University of Oxford (Minasian Collection), Tehran: Miras-e Maktoob, 2016), with further improvements.

availability.p: Entry to the Library is permitted upon presentation of a valid university ID card (for admissions procedures, please visit Wadham College Library, Persian Studies Section). Please Contact persian.library@wadham.ox.ac.ukfor further information on the availability of this manuscript.
